definitions.explanation: Describes something that shows visible signs of age or wear. Used as a pre-noun modifier (the past-tense form of the verb {古|ふる}びる, functioning adjectivally).

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}びた{本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}つけた→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧。
{古|ふる}びた⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}ぶ→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧⟦{通|とお}り→通り：01475_toori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: I walked along a street lined with weathered buildings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{古|ふる}びた⟦{家具|かぐ}→家具：12314_kagu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather's house still has a lot of worn old furniture.

notes:
USAGE:
{古|ふる}びた is the past-tense form of the verb ⟦{古|ふる}びる→古びる：11950_furubiru⟧ (to become old-looking), used as a pre-noun modifier. It describes objects that have taken on an aged appearance through the passage of time.
{古|ふる}びた is neutral — it can suggest charm and character (like antiques) or simply describe something showing wear. Compare with ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧, which simply means "old" without emphasizing the visual impression of aging.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古|ふる}びた⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧ (a weathered building)
- {古|ふる}びた⟦{写真|しゃしん}→写真：00753_shashin⟧ (an old-looking photo)
- {古|ふる}びた{街並|まちな}み (an aged townscape)
